subject: Performance SLO qualification - latency & cost levers (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme-ai.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap and next steps

Alex / Sophie - thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a couple of asks so our infra team can size an initial recommendation. PDF + sample latency traces attached.

Recap (what I heard):
- Target latency: p95 <= 150-200 ms for single-turn completions (up to ~512 tokens).
- Throughput: average 600 req/s, peak ~1,200 req/s.
- Concurrency: up to 400 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Streaming: yes - you need early partial tokens (chunked streaming) for UX.
- Quality floor: prefer model A (highest quality) for 18% of traffic (fraud-check/high-sensitivity), cheaper model B for the rest.
- Budget: looking to keep inference spend < $X/month (we discussed ballpark; confirm).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the p50/p95 targets and whether the 512-token cap is the right estimate for worst-case responses?
2) Please attach a 24-hour representative trace (RPS over time + sample request/response token lengths). The latency_samples.csv attached is an example of the format that helps us.
3) Are there any hard constraints around cold-starts / warm instance time (e.g., must be < 500ms)?

What we'll propose after we get the trace: a recommended config that balances cost & latency - likely a mixed-variant routing plan plus continuous batching, prefix/KV caching for repeat contexts, and an int8 quantized profile for the cheaper model. We'll also run a short perf test with your sample traces to validate p95 numbers.

Proposed meeting: tech deep-dive with Rishi (runtime) and Marcus (solutions) - can you do Mon/Tue next week?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme_slo_requirements.pdf, latency_samples.csv

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme-ai.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa - confirmed and a few clarifications below. I attached the 24h trace (see latency_samples.csv) - let me know if you need a longer window.

Confirmed numbers:
- p95 target: <= 150 ms (we're aiming for 150, ideally lower). p50 target: <= 30 ms.
- Worst-case token length: 512 tokens (very rare), median response ~140 tokens.
- Peak throughput (short bursts): up to ~1,200 req/s; steady-state expected ~600 req/s.
- Peak concurrency: 400 simultaneous sessions - many of these will be streaming sessions where tokens arrive incrementally.
- Streaming: required. We need partial tokens to appear client-side within ~50-75 ms of generation (i.e., low inter-chunk latency).
- Budget: we're not ready to share exact $ target publicly in the thread - but aim to keep infra costs predictable and lower than our current provider by at least 20%.

Other constraints:
- Data residency: all inference must run in US regions.
- Security: SOC2 report requested (we have that from your portal).

We can do the tech deep-dive Tuesday (23rd) 10:00 AM PT if that works for your team. Rishi / Marcus on the invite will be great.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme AI
alex.johnson@acme-ai.com
+1 (206) 555-0142

Attachments: latency_samples.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Sophie Lee <sophie.lee@acme-ai.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLO qualification - post-call recap and next steps

Perfect - thanks for the trace and the clear targets. Looping in Rishi (runtime) and Marcus (solutions) to propose an initial config and perf-test plan. High-level recommendations up front so you have context before the dive: 

1) Mixed-variant routing (cost vs quality):
   - Primary: quantized medium-size variant (redwood-sparrow-medium-int8) for ~82% of traffic.
   - Fallback/high-quality: redwood-sparrow-large (fp16) for ~18% of traffic and critical flows.

2) Quantization profile: int8 for cheaper variant (validated for your workloads in our internal evals). Keep large model in fp16 for quality-critical paths.

3) Continuous batching + smart routing:
   - Continuous batching will aggregate short windows (1-5ms) to increase GPU utilization without blowing inter-chunk latency for streaming.
   - For streaming, we'll prioritize low inter-chunk latency by dynamically batching smaller micro-batches for streaming sessions and larger batches for non-streaming.

4) Prefix/KV caching:
   - Use KV cache for repeated contexts (search/chat histories) to avoid re-computing prefixes - should shave p95 for repeat flows by ~20-40% depending on hit rate.

5) Autoscaling & dedicated pools:
   - Recommend Dedicated capacity for predictable p95 targets at your scale. We can provision reserved GPU pools with burst capacity for peak spikes.

6) Perf test plan:
   - We'll replay your 24h trace against the proposed config (quantized medium + fp16 fallback) and capture p50/p95, inter-chunk latencies, and cost estimates.
   - Deliverable: perf report + recommended instance types, batching params, and cost-per-1k-tokens estimate.

Next steps: Marcus/Rishi - can you take the trace and produce an initial perf run (48-72h turnaround)? Alex/Sophie - confirm Tue 10:00 AM PT and we'll send calendar invite with a short agenda (15-30m).

Thanks - looking forward to the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
